The game is complete. **`snake_zai-glm-5.3_01.html`** (831 lines, ~24 KB) — a fully self-contained Snake game with zero external dependencies.

**What's inside:**

- **Classic Snake on a 30×30 grid** — canvas-rendered with HiDPI scaling, subtle checkerboard, rounded snake segments with fading tails, heads with directional eyes, and pulsing food with glow.
- **Three game modes** (selectable from the start menu via keys `1`/`2`/`3` or clicking):
  - **Human vs Human** — P1 (green) on WASD, P2 (orange) on arrow keys
  - **CPU vs Human** — you play the orange snake (arrows *or* WASD) against a CPU
  - **CPU vs CPU** — spectate two AIs racing for food
- **CPU AI** — BFS pathfinding to food, with fallback strategies: tail-following for survival, then free-neighbor selection ranked by flood-fill space. Every move is safety-simulated (can the snake still reach its tail afterward?), and it avoids head-on collision cells against equal-or-longer opponents.
- **Faithful 2-snake collision rules** — simultaneous tick resolution: walls, self-bites, crashing into the opponent (with correct tail-vacates exemption), head-on same-cell collisions (both die), plus mutual head-swaps.
- **Live score bar** — colored panels for both snakes with names, scores, and grayscale on death; game-over screen shows the death reason, the winner (or tie), and final scores.
- **Full keypress flow** — `1/2/3` pick a mode, `P` pauses, `R` restarts instantly, `Enter`/`Space`/`R` restarts from game over, `Esc` returns to the menu. Arrow/space default scrolling is suppressed.
- **Arcade pacing** — starts at 115 ms/tick, speeds up by 2 ms per food eaten (floor 60 ms), driven by an rAF accumulator with tab-switch dt clamping.

Open the file in any browser and press `1`, `2`, or `3` to play.

{"edit_description":"Create a NEW file `snake_zai-glm-5.3_01.html` — a complete, self-contained classic Snake battle game (HTML + CSS + JS in one file, no external resources, no network requests, system fonts only). All code and comments in English. Implement EXACTLY this spec:

## Visual design
- Dark neon arcade theme: page background radial gradient #0b1020 → #05070d; accent #38bdf8; text #e2e8f0; muted #64748b. Center the app column on screen.
- Layout top-to-bottom: header with title "SNAKE" (gradient text) + subtitle "30 × 30 ARENA"; score bar; board wrapper; footer hint line "P pause · R restart · ESC menu".
- Score bar: CSS grid `1fr auto 1fr` width matching board: left panel = snake 1, center = mode label (e.g. "CPU VS HUMAN"), right panel = snake 2. Each panel: colored dot, player name, monospace bold score value pushed to the right (margin-left:auto). A dead snake's panel gets class `dead` (grayscale filter, opacity .45).
- Board: logical 600×600 canvas, 30×30 grid, cell 20px. Scale canvas by devicePixelRatio (canvas.width = 600*dpr, ctx.scale(dpr,dpr), CSS width:100%, display:block). Wrapper width min(600px, 92vmin), position:relative, rounded corners, glow box-shadow.
- Three absolutely-positioned overlays covering the board (start menu, pause, game over), background rgba(5,8,15,.85) + backdrop blur, flex-centered content, toggled with a `.hidden{display:none}` class.
- Start menu: heading, then three clickable buttons (full-width, hover glow) each showing a key badge and description:
  [1] Human vs Human — P1: WASD · P2: Arrow keys
  [2] CPU vs Human — You (orange) vs CPU, arrows or WASD
  [3] CPU vs CPU — watch the machines duel
  Plus a small controls summary.
- Game-over overlay: "GAME OVER" heading, one-line death reason, winner line (e.g. "PLAYER 2 WINS!" colored with the winner's color, or "IT'S A TIE!"), final score line like "PLAYER 1 · 30 40 · PLAYER 2", hint "[ENTER] play again · [ESC] menu".
- Pause overlay: "PAUSED", "[P] resume · [ESC] menu".

## Data model
- Constants GRID=30, CELL=20, SIZE=600. Directions are {x,y} objects.
- `state` ∈ MENU / RUNNING / PAUSED / OVER. `mode` ∈ 'hh' | 'ch' | 'cc'.
- MODES config:
  - hh: [PLAYER 1, human, keys 'wasd', green, left start facing right], [PLAYER 2, human, keys 'arrows', orange, right start facing left]
  - ch: [CPU, cpu, green, left], [YOU, human, keys 'both' (arrows AND wasd both accepted), orange, right]
  - cc: [CPU 1, cpu, green], [CPU 2, cpu, orange]
- Snake object: `{ body:[{x,y}...] head-first, dir, queue:[], cpu, keys, name, idx, score, alive }`. Start length 4. Snake 1: head (8,8), body extends left, dir {1,0}. Snake 2: head (21,21), body extends right, dir {-1,0}.
- Colors: snake 1 body #22c55e head #4ade80; snake 2 body #f97316 head #fb923c; dead body #475569 head #64748b. Food #ef4444.
- Single food {x,y} spawned on a random free cell (never on any snake). If no free cell exists → end game, winner = higher score (tie if equal).

## Game loop
- One requestAnimationFrame render loop. Logic ticks via time accumulator (dt = clamped to 250ms) only while state === RUNNING. `interval = Math.max(60, 115 - totalFoodEaten * 2)` ms.

## Tick order (critical, implement exactly)
1. Per snake: if cpu → direction = AI choice; else if queue non-empty → dir = queue.shift().
2. Compute nextHead for both snakes.
3. Wall check: nextHead out of [0,GRID) → dead (cause "hit the wall").
4. eating[i] = nextHead equals food cell.
5. Body collisions: for each not-yet-dead snake i, scan against each snake j (j=0 and 1): j's body cells 0..len-1 EXCLUDING j's tail cell when !eating[j] (the tail vacates unless that snake grows this tick); hit → dead[i]. Cause: i===j ? "bit its own tail" : `crashed into ${snakes[1-i].name}`.
6. If neither dead and both nextHeads are the same cell → both dead, cause "head-on collision". (Mutual head-swap deaths are already caught by step 5 because each head enters the other's current head cell.)
7. If any dead: set alive=false for them, build a reason string from the causes, winner = survivor or tie if both dead, state = OVER, show overlay, update panels. Do NOT move any snake on the death tick.
8. Otherwise apply movement: body.unshift(nextHead); if eating → score += 10, totalFoodEaten++, spawn new food, recompute interval; else body.pop(). Update score panels.

## Input (document keydown, use e.code; always preventDefault for Arrow keys and Space)
- MENU: Digit1/Numpad1 → start 'hh'; Digit2 → 'ch'; Digit3 → 'cc'.
- OVER: Enter / Space / KeyR → restart same mode; Escape → back to menu.
- RUNNING: KeyP → toggle pause; KeyR → instant restart same mode; Escape → menu; otherwise dispatch movement keys to non-CPU snakes by their `keys` ('wasd': KeyW/A/S/D; 'arrows': ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right; 'both': check both maps).
- Direction queue pushDir(snake, dir): compare against last queued dir (or current dir if queue empty); ignore if same or exact reverse (prevents 180° flip); cap queue at 3. This allows fast double-turns safely.
- PAUSED: KeyP resumes; Escape → menu.

## CPU AI (per tick, per CPU snake, against the other snake)
Helpers: `k(x,y)` string key; `inBounds(c)`; `bfs(start, goal, blockedSet)` returns path array (start..goal) or null; `floodCount(start, blockedSet)` = count of reachable free cells via BFS; `reachable(a, b, blocked)` = BFS existence check. IMPORTANT: clone blocked Sets before deleting keys (e.g. tail-follow needs own tail removed).
Priority of candidate cells:
1. First step of BFS path from head to food (blocked = ALL body cells of both snakes).
2. First step of BFS path from head to own tail (blocked = same set minus own tail key).
3. All in-bounds unblocked neighbor cells EXCLUDING the reverse of current direction, sorted by floodCount descending.
Safety simulation isSafeStep(step): build newBody = [step, ...(old body, keeping tail only if step is food)]; blocked2 = other snake's full body + newBody[1..]; safe if reachable(step, newTail, blocked2) OR floodCount(step, blocked2) >= newBody.length + 1.
headOnRisk(step): opponent head within Manhattan distance 1 of step AND opponent length >= own length.
Choose first candidate passing isSafeStep && !headOnRisk; else first passing isSafeStep; else keep current direction. (BFS paths can never reverse into the neck because the neck is blocked.)

## Rendering (every frame)
- Checkerboard: cells (x+y)%2 ? #101a2b : #0c1524.
- Food (only when a game exists, not in MENU): pulsing circle, radius ~6 + sin pulse using timestamp (t/300), radial gradient glow.
- Snakes: rounded-rect segments inset 1px in the cell (write a manual roundedRect helper — do NOT rely on ctx.roundRect), alpha fading toward tail (clamp min ~0.35), head drawn slightly brighter/larger with two eyes (white sclera + dark pupils) offset forward+lateral based on dir. Dead snakes drawn in gray tones.
- In MENU state draw just the empty checkerboard (overlay covers it anyway).

## Misc
- startGame(mode): fully reset snakes/food/scores/queue/totalFoodEaten/interval, set panel names + mode label, hide overlays, state=RUNNING. toMenu(): state=MENU, show menu overlay.
- No redeclaration bugs, no unused globals, clean section comments. Show menu overlay on load, start the rAF loop immediately.","path":"snake_zai-glm-5.3_01.html"}
